best_for: Developers and DBAs who run MySQL and want Oracle's own free desktop tool for queries, user grants and slow-query checks.
description:
MySQL Workbench Community Edition is Oracle's free desktop tool for people who build and run MySQL databases, from developers to DBAs and database architects. It is GPL-licensed, and Oracle says the current release works with every MySQL Server version it still supports.

GUI plugin examples show you how to add your own workflows to the app. Each download comes with a GnuPG signature and an MD5 checksum, so you can check that the file you got is the real one. When you get stuck, there are MySQL forums, a Workbench blog and a public bug tracker. The old MySQL GUI Tools bundle, with Administrator and Query Browser, has reached end of life, so Workbench is the tool to use in its place.

points.title: Not 8.0 anymore
points.text: The current release is 26.10.0, rebuilt on MySQL Shell. It replaces both the old Workbench and the retired MySQL Shell for VS Code, so expect a different look if you remember 8.0.

points.title: Write SQL, see the plan
points.text: The script editor and SQL notebooks support auto-complete, formatting and editing results in place. Notebooks also run JavaScript and TypeScript, and Visual Explain shows how a query was run.

points.title: Server admin in the same window
points.text: You can check server status and settings, manage users and grants, and look at client connections. Performance reports cover slow queries, table sizes, memory and waits.

points.title: Some parts lean on paid Oracle products
points.text: Visual backup works with MySQL Enterprise Backup, and the migration assistant targets HeatWave on Oracle Cloud. The Community Edition itself is GPL and free.

points.title: Windows needs extra runtimes
points.text: Oracle lists .NET Framework 4.5 and the Visual C++ 2019 redistributable as prerequisites for the x64 MSI, which installs machine-wide.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 4 versions. Mac has separate Intel and Apple Silicon DMGs, with only the current release listed. Older builds are on Oracle's archive page.
